summary.title: How to Write a Video Player in Less Than 1000 Lines
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a working C video player using ffmpeg for decoding and SDL for audio and video output, in under 1000 lines of code.
keywords: write a video player in c
takeaways: ffmpeg handles decoding, encoding, muxing and demuxing, so a player can focus on moving data between components.
SDL is used to output the audio and video of the media file.
The tutorial builds up in stages, starting from an updated version of Martin Böhme's original tutorial and moving toward a player based on Fabrice Bellard's ffplay.c.
Each stage comes with a downloadable C source file that can be compiled and followed along.
Readers are expected to know C and basic concepts such as queues and mutexes; multimedia basics are explained along the way.
summary.summary: This is a multi-part tutorial by Dranger that walks through writing a complete video player in C using the ffmpeg libraries for decoding and SDL for audio and video output. It explains that existing ffmpeg documentation was sparse, so the author documents learning the library as they go. Each lesson introduces one or two new ideas and provides a C source file to compile and follow along with, modeled on the sample ffplay player.
